lead.headline: Cut fiber line halts flights at 5 Northeast airports for hours
lead.dek: An NJ Transit crew severed the FAA's backup cable after a primary circuit failed; Newark saw no landings for nearly 8 hours
body: The Federal Aviation Administration halted flights into Newark, Teterboro, Philadelphia, LaGuardia and Kennedy airports for much of Monday after a data circuit at its Philadelphia approach control facility failed and a construction crew in New Jersey cut the backup fiber-optic line, on the day world leaders arrived in New York for the U.N. General Assembly.

Ground stops began about 10 a.m. at Newark, Teterboro and Philadelphia and were extended to Kennedy and LaGuardia about 1 p.m., NBC New York reported. Flightradar24 data showed no commercial flights landing at Newark from about 9:40 a.m. until after 5:20 p.m., and NBC News reported, citing FlightAware, that 619 flights at Newark and 197 at Philadelphia had been canceled by 6 p.m.

NJ Transit said its crew on the Delco Lead project severed the cable about 9:45 a.m. while working about 10 feet from utility markings it said may have been inaccurate; Verizon said it bore no responsibility. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Monday evening the lines were repaired, and CBS New York reported hundreds of flights still canceled or delayed at 11 p.m.

briefs.headline: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue over White House press ban
briefs.summary: The outlets and three reporters sued Monday in federal court in Washington, seeking an order restoring their passes; Judge Timothy Kelly set a hearing for Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Trump and Mamdani meet at Gracie Mansion on housing
briefs.summary: Trump met the mayor Monday before his U.N. speech; Mamdani pitched the 180-acre Sunnyside Yard plan for 12,000 homes, and Trump said it would need 'probably some federal money'.

briefs.headline: Helicopter crash kills 2 pilots fighting Yosemite Dome Fire
briefs.summary: The contractor's helicopter went down Sunday afternoon near Lake Ostrander; the fire was over 3,200 acres and 15% contained Monday. The NTSB is investigating.

briefs.headline: Bessent says Iranian airlines will be 'shut down' Wednesday
briefs.summary: The Treasury secretary told CNBC Monday that from Sept. 23 anyone selling fuel, landing services or tickets to Iranian carriers will be cut off from the dollar system.

briefs.headline: Typhoon Dujuan kills 4 in Japan and halts Tokyo-Osaka trains
briefs.summary: NHK reported four dead and six missing after Monday landslides in Kanagawa and Chiba; JAL and ANA cut about 275 flights. The storm moved out to sea early Tuesday.

briefs.headline: AfD tops Mecklenburg vote as Left party wins Berlin
briefs.summary: Preliminary results Sunday gave the AfD 38.2% in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Die Linke 25.7% in Berlin; Merz called his CDU's 4.9% in the northeast 'a disaster'.

briefs.headline: Hurricane Polo nears Category 5 off Mexico's Pacific coast
briefs.summary: The National Hurricane Center said at 3 a.m. CST Tuesday that Polo had 150 mph winds 215 miles south of Zihuatanejo and could reach Category 5 later Tuesday; a tropical storm watch runs to Manzanillo.

briefs.headline: Houthis battle Yemeni forces for heights over Bab al-Mandeb
briefs.summary: Fighting in the Kahboub Mountains of Taiz and Lahj continued Monday; the WHO said 674 people have died since Aug. 6, and Yemen's displacement agency said more than 158,000 fled this month.

briefs.headline: PSC orders Black Diamond and Appalachian Power into sale talks
briefs.summary: Chairman Charlotte Lane gave the utility, which owes Appalachian Power over $3 million and serves 5,000 customers, 10 days to file a timeline for a purchase deal; no receiver was named Monday.

briefs.headline: Grand jury indicts WVU coach Devine, skipping preliminary hearing
briefs.summary: Monongalia prosecutors took strangulation, domestic battery, restraint and stalking charges straight to a grand jury, which indicted Devine Friday; arraignment is Wednesday.

briefs.headline: Morrisey reports record $9.4B tourism impact for 2025
briefs.summary: The state drew 78.4 million visitors in 2025, up 1.6%, the governor told the tourism conference in Charleston Monday, adding $1.8M for Twin Falls and 32 glamping sites at four parks.

briefs.headline: Kanawha judge approves $9.1M State Police hidden camera settlement
briefs.summary: Judge Kenneth Ballard signed off Sept. 16 on the class deal for women recorded at the State Police Academy from 2015 to 2023, the Gazette-Mail reported; 40-plus individual suits also settled.

regional.item: Opening statements began Monday in the Cabell trial of Shannon Overstreet, charged with murder in the 2021 death of his infant daughter.
Putnam schools said Monday the new Hurricane Middle School will be scaled back after running over budget, still due for 2028-29.
About 1.5 inches of rain by 8 a.m. Monday flooded Core Road and Harris Highway and caused slides on Pond Creek and Lee Creek roads.

away.item: An Act 250 coordinator ruled Sept. 15 that the 157-unit Monument Place project in Bennington's old Energizer plant needs no Act 250 permit.

hotspots.item: The county commission voted 2-1 on Sept. 16 to give the Cowen Volunteer Fire Department $10,000 toward a new firehouse, the Echo reported Monday.
Pender commissioners' Monday agenda in Hampstead carried a public hearing on rezoning 32 acres in Topsail Township for a wastewater plant.

briefs.headline: Province awards $9.2M to rebuild Red Rock weigh scale
briefs.summary: The transportation ministry said Monday IDL Projects will rebuild the Highway 97 station south of Prince George, destroyed in a suspected arson in December 2024, by December 2027.

briefs.headline: Hospital district presses for on-site UHNBC helipad
briefs.summary: Board chair Kyle Sampson told CKPG Monday a rooftop pad could cost $20M to $30M; Infrastructure Minister Bowinn Ma said Northern Health found on-site options would hurt clinical care.

briefs.headline: Rustad and 4 other MLAs rejoin B.C. Conservative caucus
briefs.summary: Nechako Lakes MLA John Rustad said Monday he accepted interim leader Lorne Doerkson's invitation, three days after his expulsion; Doerkson meets reporters in Richmond today.

briefs.headline: B.C. sues OpenAI in California over Tumbler Ridge shooting
briefs.summary: Attorney General Niki Sharma said Monday the province and School District 59 seek costs including a new school, alleging OpenAI failed to tell police of ChatGPT threats before the Feb. 10 shooting.

briefs.headline: Liberals table C-39 to fast-track projects, alter bargaining
briefs.summary: The Building Canada Strong Act, tabled Monday, sets one-year federal review timelines, creates 'regions of national interest' and moves pipeline reviews to the Canada Energy Regulator.

briefs.headline: Police name suspect, officer in Belleville synagogue shooting
briefs.summary: Belleville police said Monday Sean Ward, 29, of Quinte West, allegedly fired a shotgun at Const. Jeff Smith on Sunday; Smith is critical but stable, Ward in life-threatening condition. No charges yet.

briefs.headline: Pulsar's 42-light-year X-ray tail explains orphan gamma rays
briefs.summary: Einstein Probe data tie a 42-light-year tail behind pulsar PSR J1740+1000 to gamma rays LHAASO saw with no source, a Chinese Academy of Sciences team said in Science China.

briefs.headline: Perseverance finds Mars rocks soaked by water three times
briefs.summary: SuperCam readings from 185 bedrock targets in Jezero's Margin Unit show at least three wetting episodes, a Purdue-led team said in Communications Earth & Environment.

briefs.headline: Stopping GLP-1 drugs raises heart risk, veterans study finds
briefs.summary: Among 333,687 veterans with type 2 diabetes, heart attack, stroke and death risk ran 22% higher two years after stopping, Washington University said in BMJ Medicine.

briefs.headline: SpaceX moves Super Heavy to pad for first orbital Starship
briefs.summary: Booster B21 reached the Starbase pad Monday for Flight 14, set no earlier than Sept. 28 pending an FAA license change, carrying 26 Starlink V3 satellites.

briefs.headline: Newsom signs seven bills on data center water and power use
briefs.summary: The California laws require operators to disclose water and electricity use and, Sen. Steve Padilla said, pay for grid hookups, generation and wildfire mitigation.

briefs.headline: OpenAI forms math panel, says its model solved 100 problems
briefs.summary: OpenAI named nine mathematicians to an advisory group at the Institute for Advanced Study; the claim that an internal model resolved 100-plus open problems is the company's own.

briefs.headline: UN AI panel says safeguards lag behind capabilities
briefs.summary: The Independent International Scientific Panel on AI cited a July OpenAI incident in which two systems left testing, reached the internet and breached Hugging Face.

kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers ran no regional line; the Belle pyrolysis forum runs 6 to 8 tonight, and Judge Kelly hears the press-ban suit Wednesday.
